title: Decide on configuration file format: TOML vs YAML vs JSON
description: We need to finalize the configuration file format for project settings and dependency constraints. In python packaging, pyproject.toml is standard, but some contributors requested YAML for compatibility with existing CI templates. Let's debate the options and commit to a single standard.
author: charliermarsh

comments.author: dev-contributor-alex
comments.body: I propose we use YAML (.uv.yaml). Almost all devops tools, GitHub Actions, and Kubernetes use YAML. Contributors are already familiar with the indentation syntax.

comments.author: security-auditor-eva
comments.body: I strongly object to YAML. YAML is notoriously difficult to parse securely due to arbitrary type coercion and code execution CVEs in standard parsers. Furthermore, the Norway problem ('NO' interpreted as boolean False) causes silent parsing bugs in configuration.

comments.author: frontend-dev-sam
comments.body: What about JSON? It has zero ambiguity, is supported natively in every programming language, and serde_json is blazing fast.

comments.author: maintainer-marcus
comments.body: JSON is disqualified because configuration files need comments. Forcing developers to maintain machine-only JSON with no comments for complex build options is a terrible developer experience.

comments.author: charliermarsh
comments.body: I propose standardizing on TOML. It aligns with PEP 518/PEP 621 (pyproject.toml), has unambiguous typing, first-class comment support, and serde integrations in Rust are very mature. We will read from [tool.uv] in pyproject.toml and fallback to uv.toml.

comments.author: dev-contributor-alex
comments.body: Fair enough. Given the Python ecosystem conventions and security considerations Eva mentioned, TOML makes complete sense. I withdraw the YAML proposal.

comments.author: maintainer-marcus
comments.body: Consensus reached: We accept TOML as the single official configuration format. Rejected YAML due to security vulnerabilities and typing ambiguities. Rejected JSON due to absence of comment support. Implemented in PR #1045.
